So glad I get to be one of the first people to post a review on here and also a little bit concerned that there aren’t more reviews. I feel like this is a legit game that should be blowing up right now.

Look, the game has its issues and it’s in early access so it’s got a lot of unfinished content and a few bugs and glitches sure. But for the most part this game is great.

I mainly give it a thumbs up because it does what it sets out to do. A cowboy simulator that actually makes you feel immersed and feel like you’re accurately simulating being a cowboy on the frontier. Or at least a settler on the frontier.

Regardless the game has an overabundance of positives in comparison to its negatives therefore it gets a nice big thumbs up from me.

Just briefly, the game has great gameplay, great sound design, great premise, tons of content, it all flows and works well and feels comfortable and cohesive. It’s open ended, open world, with quests, jobs, gunslinging, cattle wrestling, farming, building, crafting, cooking, dialogue options, reputation, horse riding, trapping. I think the only thing missing is relationships and fishing.

They add those in and fix its stability issues and this game is gonna be awesome.

I really liked it, and couldn’t really think of much to say negatively against it. Even that price tag is super affordable and you’re NOT getting ripped off. I think the biggest negative going against it is simple, it’s unfinished. That’s it. Otherwise it’s hard to think of anything bad about the game to make mention of.

But if you’d like a more in-depth look at the game with gameplay and more information I’d encourage you to check out the review on my YouTube Channel (link below).

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b6RAfhvSWCI

Otherwise, thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.

An exceptionally strong start from an EA title.

I started this game thinking it would be comparable to the absolute tonne of other early access games slapping the "Simulator" title on the end of their name - most of which I ended up refunding because of bugs, lack of content, or just a really jank feeling to things. I was ready for the cringe vibes the second I started it.

But, this game was really surprising for me. Off the bat, it runs great, looks great, animations seem good, and the voice acting of the lead character is actually really good - a choice which most sims either don't do, or do poorly. 

The setting is very nice, the map seems crafted well and feels vast. The UI is probably the best I have seen for a title just released to EA, and really does well in building your confidence in its development - the devs have clearly considered polishing the game up for its EA release. Rather than just saying the words, they have actually made it presentable, and don't seem to be peddling a product with a million "oh we'll fix this and that" promises. It's already simple and enjoyable to play.

There's already a tonne of unlockables, crafting things, quests, and things that'll give you plenty of enjoyment, and I already feel an itch to play more after this review. The amount of content for the current price is awesome - I've paid more for other EA games which i've been happy with, with alot less content. 

You can see the directions which the devs are going in from alot of the crafting menus etc. which is nice, and i'm sure ill be coming back with each update. 

If you like early access journeys, this game is one to be a part of!

Well, it's another Early Access title.  Can you trust it?  With so many companies throwing out trashfires and then bailing on their players, it's a very important question.
So far, the answer is yes.
The game went through a trial, then a playtest, and is now in Early Access.  Each phase was introduced with more content, more stability, and more enjoyment.  The developers are active here on Steam and, especially, in the Discord.  They communicate and listen.
The game itself is actually quite good considering it is on Day 1 of Early Access.  There's enough to do, enough to explore, and quite fun.  Sure, it's got the standard Early Access bugs and limitations, but, for the price being asked, it's a worthwhile investment.  I already have 70 hours in pre-release testing and had a hell of a good time playing.
There are still some considerations.  There's no controller support.  No female protagonist.  The story and map are both incomplete.  For some, these are deal breakers but the developers have already indicated that all of these are in the process of being addressed and added into the game.  So, if those are holding you back, they won't for long.
In a nutshell, yes, it's Early Access but it's a hell of a lot better than most of the things out there.
And if you're coming here after the bad taste of Wild West Dynasty still in your mouth, this may be the mouthwash you need to finally be rid of it.  It's about 50 times better in Early Access than WWD will ever be.

I don’t usually play early access games, but I did want to take a chance on this one as the wild west is a weakness of mine. 

So far, I’ve had tons of fun! I think the game looks gorgeous and I often find myself just riding around looking at it. I’m the type of gamer who loves exploring the map, and I’ve come across some fun nooks and crannies with interesting finds in the landscape! I hope the map is expanded in future updates. 

A lot of other comments have mentioned bugs, but so far, I have only come across one. The ground vanished and I fell into the abyss. But after a restart, it never happened again. 

I have about 500 hours in Stardew Valley and 200+ hours in other various farming games, so I’m pleased there is farming. The crops are very detailed and pretty to look at, and I do like the watering system they have here. It’s not just a one-and-done, crops have a water meter you can fill, or let drain that (seemingly) only affects quality of the crops. As of yet, I haven’t had any crops fail. So you can go riding around or questing (or in my case, die to bandits 3 days in a row) and you will still have crops to harvest, they just won’t be the best. It gives you an incentive to come back and do a little watering rather than staying out all day and that’s a nice change from a water-and-forget that most farming games have. 

Animal husbandry/ranching is a bit more hit-and-miss. Personally, I love having a mess of animals around to pet and watch. Makes it feel like a real ranch. However, as of this writing, you can’t interact, or even really see, your rabbits. A hutch can hold 8, and I went out of my way to capture a bunch of them and pick one of each color to add, only to find out once the rabbits are in, you can’t see them. The hutch’s lattice is too condensed. You MIGHT catch a glimpse of a rabbit maybe running around or standing up and sniffing, but not well. Also as of writing, the chicken coop can’t be seen into, and chickens seem to be unaffected by fences, so they just wander off into the wilderness where they become cryptids that you’re likely never to see ever again. I only know my chicken is still alive because eggs keep showing up. Cows and goats wander around being adorable and are not able to phase through fences like their chicken counterparts. I love that, and I enjoy petting and listening to them as I work. 

As of this writing, animal breeding is not fully implemented, so if you want an animal, you have to hope the animal seller NPC has the one you want in their rotating stock. I hope in the future you are able to buy or trade animals with the other ranches/farmers near you, or, even better, find them in the wild. Maybe even a “russtler” option where if you go out in the night, you can steal an animal. 

There is also currently one horse in one color. I’d like to be able to build a stable and have more. Or, at the very least, get the option to choose my horse color when you buy the one and only horse. 

The crafting system is also pretty good. There is a wide array of things to craft for early access, but there are a lot of the advanced items that are not yet available. Nothing that you desperately need in the first dozen hours of the game, so I don’t think them being currently locked affects the enjoyment of the early game. There’s nothing really wrong with the crafting system that I’ve come across, my only issue is that once a building is placed, you can’t move it. I’m a player that likes to have things a certain way, and my first attempt is not always the best so I like to be able to adjust them. Be careful where you build your buildings, you won’t be able to move them!!

I only have 2 “major” gripes so far, one of which was already addressed in the first patch, and one that may be addressed as more content is added up to the full release. 

1. Bandit encounters. I’m not a big FPS gamer, so this part isn’t for me, BUT what would a cowboy game be without gun fights? I’m glad they are here, however, I am getting frustrated with their frequency. As an explorer type gamer, I like aimlessly running around looking at things. And that seemed to trigger endless encounters. About every 5-10 minutes of wandering, another encounter. At first, it’s one bandit, I can handle that, then two, okay, I can do that, next is three, okay that’s annoying and I’m starting to die, and then (up to this writing) four bandits at a time with rifles and double-barreled shot guns. Now I can’t survive as the second you fire, a bandit fans the hammer of their revolver on you and now you’re down to 25% health. One more hit and you’re done for. Hope you are in a place that has cover, and that cover that is tall enough to shield you while standing since there is no crouch. 

I got so fed up with it, the only path into the main town I found that I could get through without yet another tier 4 bandit encounter was through the out of the way, long train tunnel where my horse catches on invisible barriers and can’t really gallop through. But I never take any other route because it’s the only safe one I have. 

With the first patch, they did give us an “easy” mode where you only take 1 damage from bandits. You are most likely not going to die anymore and I, as a cozy gamer who would rather not gunfight, like that. BUT I’ve found the encounters still happen all the time and that keeps me from my quests and plans. I have to constantly stop, get off my horse, gun fight, get back on my horse, and continue. I wish you could “gallop” through the encounter if you don’t want to deal with bandits, or if you want to, you can stop your horse and engage with the mechanic. 

2. Lack of “side” activities. They do have a good amount of side quests for early access, but there isn’t much in the way of other activities aside from watering crops and resource gathering. Right now, there isn’t much to do in the game other than the main and side quests. So if you burn through those quickly, you’re going to be waiting until the next content drop for a reason to log back in. 

I’d like to see more wild animals you can hunt (right now I have only run into boars). Deer, elk, coyotes, bison, ducks, turkeys, bears, bob cats. Their pelts can make different types of leather or meats, or they have different components you could use in building or decorating. 

I know gamers in general are torn about fishing mechanics, but come on. We are in the wild west with a log cabin by a lake, fishing would go so hard AND make sense in this setting. Different fish can be in different areas of the map encouraging exploration.

Horrible game, great premise. Starting with the save system.  There are no individual save files.  It has a single save file, and if you die especially at the hands of bandits, they rob you and you have no option to do anything other than to go back to the nearest safe point and start the game back up minus your items.  The quest system is clunky.  In one case, you have to meet one of the other farmers at a place he supposedly marked on the map for you..  There is no such place on the map and you have a time window to meet up with him. If you fail it, you have to set up a new meeting with him, but he isn't at the same place where the original meeting was set up.  The NPC's sound almost like the Swedish chef on the muppets and move in odd angles that look like someone having a seizure.  The building system is based on your progression, however, getting the money, and items needed to actually build anything outside the basic things is a major grind. Between getting killed by boars, bandits, starvation, thirst, or spending all your time trying to take care of the goat your saddled with near the start of the game the game is far from pleasant and lacks a realistic curve for progression.

Not sure what it is with wild west/cowboy games.  It seems no studio can make a proper bugfree FUN game.
We have the worst in the genre in the last couple of years, Wild West Dynasty,  and then we have this one.
Now I'm not comparing those two games.   But if I were, this one is better.  BUT it also lacks some fun stuff that WWD actually has (dynasty, workers, etc).   But it looks like THIS game will eventually allow you to have workers on your ranch? Dunno, I remember seeing a building called workers lodge or something. It's of course "not available in early access" - like so many other buildings and..stuff.


But back to this game,,
For a simulator, attempting to be realistic (dont call it simulator if you dont aim for realism),   this game has many, maaany immersion-breaking 'features'.  Selfcrafting workstations.
And the best of all, UFOs !   Yes, we all know UFOs are very common on our night sky.

When you start,  you have barely anything.  You got the old boring trope of you were given/inherited a 'farm/ranch'  it's yours now good luck.
When you arrive - and this is a minor spoiler of the first 5-10 minutes and basically the premise of the game -    
you find that the farm you got/bought/whatever has burned down.   So again, we have to build from the ground up ourselves. Never seen THAT in these games before (sigh)

You'll eventually build your own house.  And workshop(s).     And you can have a few animals too.

You can build a chicken coop,  so you can have chicken. 
They're only good for eggs and feathers.  Because currently they dont even breed.    Which doesnt help when you have recipes and QUESTS that asks for chicken meat.  Which means, you literally have to go to the animal guy,  buy chickens, just to butcher them right away.   Forget breeding chickens and butchering along the way..    Oh if this was the only issue with animals I would be pleased... but alas...this is just the beginning my friends..


You can buy or capture rabbits.  Throw them into the rabbit cage you built.  Currently rabbits dont eat, so we dont even have to waste vegetables on them.   You cannot pick them up and pet them or anything. No free-roaming, every other animal roams.  Rabbits are forever stuck in their cage, til the day you decide to butcher them.  But yes, they currently do not eat,  add that to the pile of bugs.

Then we have Goats.   At first, nothing special here, everything seems to actually function.  Female goats gives milk.  Male goats, well they're there to I assume breed the females.  And eventually be slaughtered for meat and hide(to be leather)
But apparently they cannot breed if they are assigned to the "small animal home"  (who calls it animal home??).   So you build the "Medium animal home" once you unlocked it that is.
That place fits twice as many "medium and big" animals (big being cows).     Small home fits 4 goats or two cows. Medium home fits 8 goats and 4 cows.
So, I built the medium animal home.  Assigned my THREE goats,  2 females and 1 male to one of the two "pens" in this medium animal home.     Right of the bat almost, they 'reproduced'.  Aka, they made an offspring.   Now the medium animal home has two 'nurseries' one in each pen.  That's there the baby goat (and I assume baby cow) ends up.   Can't interact with it, it's basically an non-interactable decoration.
If you check the sign where you can see and change what aninals are assigned to the pen,  I see my 3 goats, AND the baby goat in the corner of that window. And it says it will become an adult in 2.0 days.
Note, it says 2 *point* 0, not twenty.
And this is where the millionth bug happened for me.   10-11 days later,  it says the baby goat will become an adult in 1.8 days.   What the actual fudge?    I can go literal days in-game without that 'countdown' moving even 0.1.    EVEN if it's a typo and supposed to say twenty instead of 2 point 0,  it still doesnt make sense. First of all 20 days? That's almost as long as I've played the damn game, no way.  Even still,  10-12 days has passed, and it has then ticked down either 0.2 or 2 days.    Its been 10-ish days!
Oh and you cannot milk the damn goats when they're inside this big(sorry medium) animal 'home'.  You have to literally wait for the damn goat to go outside so you can milk.   Never heard of that being an issue at any point in human history, that you dont find enough space to sit NEXT to a goat and milk it in a bucket. Seriously.

Haven't even bothered with Cows.  Doubt they'll be bugfree.


Like most buildings in the game, they are stupid big.  Most of the space inside these workshop buildings , has zero use.   Workshop for example, has a workbench, and unless you upgrade it, that's all you can do in the workshop. The bench is about the size of a kitchen table. Yet the entire workshop is bigger than the f-cking house.  The Forge has 2 interactable workstations.  Could easily fit them in a closet. But nope, gotta have the building take up a LOT of space.

So you can make iron in the Forge.   Currently there's a bug (surprised?) where if you use iron scraps or w/e the game calls it, instead of iron ORE, you can make infinite iron bars.  Because the forge forgot to subtract your scraps when you use them as material.  Why bother going to the mine to mine iron, when you can use *ONE* scrap forever and ever.

Trees you cut down, actually grow back.  Usually when you load into the game for your next gaming session. (aka, chop down a tree, save, quit, load save, and voila tree is back)
Problem here though, is that the trees cares NOT where or what is in it's spot.
Trees will grow thru  buildings.   I've had a tree grow right thru my Forge.  And currently I have a tree that grew right thru one of my farmfields.   Immersion is top notch in this game..

Crafting is ok though.  It is both convinient, and immersion-breaking.  Because you can just queue up stuff to craft at the workbench, and LEAVE.  It will continue crafting the axe or whatever on it's own.  Magic !

No seasons. It never gets colder or hotter. It's either sunny, cloudy, or raining. Day, or night(dawn and dusk too).  And again not to forget, your flying spotlights during the nights (UFOs)

Some of the bugs, seems to not pop up for some people. While other bugs pop up for them, but not for me.
Another very annoying bug, that I'm not alone in having. Is what we call phantom items in inventory.
See, the game is SO buggy, that currently I have about 7 or so slots in my inventory, occupied by invisible items. I cannot use 7 slots in my inventory (that number grows every day btw).   You cannot drop it or sell it. You can sort of move it around in your inventory, but that does nothing, still takes up slots.

I've also experienced NPCs spawning from the air. Even dublications of them.  The sheriffs deputy is one example, just talked to him inside the office. Went outside, barely got out the door  and there he is, on the street in front of me.  Magic I tell ya!

NPCs dont have voice lines, they mumble. Sounds like The Sims. Fortunately you can turn this off in the settings - so thx devs.


Avoid for NOW. But keep an eye on this unpolished gem. Check back in 2026.
